newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 21.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Municipal elections next year will provide a barometer of the level of support for the government and ruling party PASOK's policies, according to Prime Minister Costas Simitis. Simitis is reported to have called on his party to organise their efforts to ensure the outcome of the elections was a "vote of confidence" for the government.
--The labour ministry has drafted new guidelines governing child labour, including restrictions on paid employment for children under the age of 15.

--The Madrid agreement between Greece and Turkey is the signal for a new chapter in Greek-Turkish relations and paves the way for a direct dialogue on the issues affecting both countries, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos says. There will be high-level meetings with the Turkish side soon but little will get done if Ankara does not resolve the issue of its claims to the Aegean islet of Imia, he adds.

--Provocative comments by Turkish deputy prime minister Bulent Ecevit in occupied Cyprus on the occasion of the 23rd anniversary of the Turkish invasion of the island have been greeted cautiously by the US State Department. Ecevit was prime minister of Turkey at the time of the invasion.
--Four farmers in the Greek-Albanian border region were kidnapped and returned safely over the weekend but the fears of abduction by armed Albanian gangs continues.

--Reports of the introduction of staggered price lists for public utilities, based on income, appear to be confirmed, along with reports that share holdings, mutual funds and incomes of between four and seven million drachmas will also face additional taxes.

--Hundreds of Athenians turned up at the Athens First Cemetery on Sunday to pay their respects to Aliki Vouyouklaki, Greece's much-loved star of stage and screen, on the first anniversary of her death.

--Businessman Mihalis Trohanas will be the focus of judicial inquiries over his business activities as the head of the SoE group of companies. Senior executives of the group will also be questioned over the case.

--Italian cruise ship Costa Classica ran aground on a sandy beach on the island of Kythira, south of the Pelopponese peninsular on Saturday, while en route to Venice. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
